title: 3D chromatin remodeling during domestication defines novel targets for crop improvement.
journal: Cell, Sep 2026 (PMID 42748920; no PMCID; Europe PMC isOpenAccess=N, hasDbCrossReferences=N). No preprint found in Europe PMC. Worked from the abstract plus repository metadata only.
data_url: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/bioproject/PRJNA1207268 (SRA study SRP562092; 'Pan-3D genome of Gossypium hirsutum', Huazhong Agricultural University; raw Hi-C FASTQ only)

verified.what_i_actually_checked: PubMed elink to GEO, SRA, BioProject and BioSample returned nothing, and the Europe PMC Annotations API returned 0 accession annotations. An NCBI BioProject search found PRJNA1207268 (registered 2025-01-07, submitter contact Xianhui Huang, secondary contact mjwang@mail.hzau.edu.cn, matching the paper's first and last authors). Its SRA runinfo, ENA filereport and full SRA XML list exactly 21 public Hi-C runs from 21 BioSamples (cultivars L122-L166). All are 12 DPA (days post-anthesis) fiber collected in Wuhan in 2022 and sequenced on DNBSEQ-T7, NCBI release 2026-02-28. Each run is 4 original FASTQ files (192.8-369.6 GB per run, 5,099.9 GB total). SRA shows spots=0 because the runs are not normalized, only stored on AWS. Zenodo, Figshare, Dryad, GitHub and NGDC (BioProject and GSA, via its search JSON API) had no processed data, contact matrices, TAD or loop tables, or phenotype tables for this study. I downloaded nothing: everything is raw FASTQ far over 50 MB.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: From the abstract only: 34 semi-wild plus 267 cultivated accessions (301 total); 105 TAD reconfigurations and 58 loop rewirings tied to fiber quality; heritability gains of 16% for strength and 20% for length; 57% of 3D signatures fixed within selective sweeps; 39 homoeologs; and YY1 named by sequence-based modeling. Not retrieved: the data availability statement, supplementary tables, and where the other ~280 accessions and the fiber phenotypes are deposited. The publisher site was not scraped. That other BioSamples are registered but private is only an inference from the ID range (21 public IDs spread across SAMN46119843-SAMN46119879).

a1_downloadable.note: Fail (checked). Only raw FASTQ is public, for 21 of the 301 accessions in PRJNA1207268. I found no processed matrices, TAD or loop calls, or phenotypes in any repository. The remaining ~280 accessions were not located in SRA, ENA or NGDC.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Fail (checked). No label table exists publicly. Per-accession TAD or loop presence would have to be built by aligning about 200 GB of Hi-C reads per accession and running TAD and loop callers. Fiber-quality phenotypes are not deposited with this BioProject.

a3_inputs_present.note: Fail (checked). Inputs are raw read pairs. Sequence windows would need a reference genome plus per-accession variant calls, and none of these is linked from the BioProject.

a4_units_stated.note: Not applicable / fail. No processed table exists to carry units (checked). Contact-frequency normalization and resolution are unknown without the methods.

a5_enough_rows.note: Fail (checked). 21 public accessions, far under 400. The paper's 301 accessions are not all public. Locus-level rows (anchors x accessions) could be large, but only after the A2 construction.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: 5,099.9 GB raw FASTQ for the 21 public runs (checked); ~70 TB for 301 if typical (extrapolated, not verified)
a6_fits_laptop.note: Fail (checked). Hi-C alignment and matrix building for a ~2.3 Gb allotetraploid genome need a cluster, not a 16 GB laptop.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Fail (checked). The paper says 301 accessions; the only located repository has 21. NCBI release is 2026-02-28 and ENA first_public is 2026-03-23.

a8_label_provenance.note: Flag (paper only). The 'TAD reconfiguration' and 'loop rewiring' labels would be caller outputs computed from Hi-C contact matrices, so they depend on the caller and its thresholds. They are not direct measurements, and the paper's choice of callers was not seen.

existing_models.name: PlantCTCIP (Plant Biotechnol J 2026, 10.1111/pbi.70586; web server plantctcip.com)
existing_models.score_and_split: CNN plus transformer predicting promoter-proximal and promoter-distal chromatin interactions in maize, rice, cotton and wheat. Reports average AUC gains of 14.56% and 9.6% over conventional models; split not stated in the abstract.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Not stated in the abstract; discussion not retrieved.

existing_models.name: GenomicLinks (NAR Genom Bioinform 2024, 10.1093/nargab/lqae123)
existing_models.score_and_split: Deep model predicting 3D chromatin loops from DNA sequence in maize. Abstract says open-source; metrics and split not in the abstract.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Abstract: 'the biology underlying chromatin loop formation in plants is poorly understood'.

existing_models.name: Sequence-based model in this paper (Huang et al., Cell 2026)
existing_models.score_and_split: Abstract says only that 'sequence-based modeling' identified YY1. No code repository found on GitHub or Zenodo.

backbone.name: PlantCaduceus (plant DNA language model on 16 angiosperm genomes; PNAS 2025, 10.1073/pnas.2421738122) or Nucleotide Transformer. AlphaGenome is trained on human and mouse tracks, so it does not apply to cotton.
backbone.hardware: Moot: labels would need cluster-scale Hi-C processing. Embedding thousands of anchor windows with a DNA language model is plausible on GPU and slow on CPU (not tested).
backbone.licence: SRA data unrestricted. Paper licence unknown (paywalled). Backbone licences not checked.

integration.partner_dataset: Cotton population resequencing and fiber-transcriptome resources (e.g., CottonMD, NAR 2023, which lists 4,180 resequenced accessions). These could supply per-accession variants and expression.
integration.join_key: Accession/cultivar ID (the SRA uses lab codes L122-L166, which need mapping to germplasm names) plus genomic coordinates on a named reference build. No mapping table was found.
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Do sequence variants at loop anchors explain which 3D contacts were rewired during cotton domestication, beyond what nearby SNPs alone predict?

controls.positive_control: None available without processed data. In principle: recover the known enrichment of the YY1 motif at anchors, as reported in the abstract.
controls.negative_control: In principle: label shuffling across accessions and a GC-content-only baseline for anchor prediction.
controls.external_validation: In principle: the cotton Hi-C sets from other tissues in the J668 tissue atlas (SRA, 2024), or maize loops (GenomicLinks). None tested.

honest_claim_h3: With the public data, nothing: 21 raw Hi-C libraries from one tissue (12 DPA fiber), one site and one year support no labelled claim until the authors' TAD and loop calls and fiber phenotypes are released.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use the DNA sequence around cotton gene regions to predict which long-range DNA folding contacts changed between wild and cultivated cotton.
plain_idea.train_on: Sequence windows at chromatin contact anchors across cotton varieties. Usable examples: unknown, because no anchor table is public and only 21 of the 301 varieties have raw reads deposited.
plain_idea.predict: Whether a folding domain boundary or loop is present in a given variety. The truth would come from Hi-C (a sequencing assay that captures which DNA pieces touch in the nucleus) on 12-day cotton fiber, processed by loop-calling software.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Cotton breeders could rank DNA edits that might rewire gene regulation for fiber length and strength. But that needs the authors' processed tables, which are not public.

ml_idea: If processed calls were released: train a frozen plant DNA language model plus a classifier head on anchor windows to predict per-accession loop or TAD-boundary presence. Hold out chromosomes and accessions, and compare against a k-mer or motif-count baseline and the YY1-motif rule. Not feasible from the current deposits.

effort.cheapest_killing_check: Done: count public runs in PRJNA1207268 and look for processed tables. The count is 21 of 301 accessions, raw FASTQ only, 5.1 TB, with no TAD, loop or phenotype tables anywhere. Revisit only if the Cell supplement (read via library access, not scraped) contains per-accession TAD and loop presence matrices plus fiber phenotypes under 50 MB.

verdict_reason: Several Part A killers fail, all checked in the repository metadata. Only 21 of the 301 accessions are public in PRJNA1207268, as raw Hi-C FASTQ (5.1 TB). No processed contact matrices, TAD or loop calls, or fiber phenotypes were found on SRA, ENA, NGDC, Zenodo, Figshare, Dryad or GitHub, so the label would have to be built on a cluster. API notes: the first ENA filereport call hung past 120 s and succeeded on retry. NGDC search results load only through its JSON API, and that API did not return PRJNA1207268 for '3D genome' queries even though the title contains the phrase.
